title: Adjust a water pressure regulator only after measuring the pattern
description: Compare static and flowing PSI, identify the exact model, and decide whether adjustment is reasonable or the system needs diagnosis.
prompt: What do the pressure readings show?
answer: One gauge reading is not enough. Static pressure, pressure under flow, and overnight peak pressure separate a set-point question from restriction, supply, or thermal expansion.
urgency: Common U.S. model ranges are not universal instructions. Stop if the adjustment is seized, leaking, undocumented, or cannot hold a stable setting.
diagramAlt: Pressure regulator with gauge locations before and after the valve
identifiers: Clockwise often raises pressure on common direct-acting models, but verify the model manual.
The gauge must be downstream of the regulator.
A large pressure drop under flow can indicate restriction rather than a low set point.

choices.label: Static PSI is high
choices.detail: Check overnight rise and thermal expansion before assuming adjustment is the only issue.

choices.label: Static PSI is normal but flow PSI collapses
choices.detail: Restriction, supply, sizing, or strainer condition may be involved.

choices.label: Pressure will not hold after adjustment
choices.detail: A service or replacement comparison is more useful than repeated turns.

steps.title: Read the model instructions
steps.body: Confirm range, direction, locknut procedure, and gauge location.

steps.title: Measure a baseline
steps.body: Record static and flowing pressure before touching the adjustment.

steps.title: Make only documented changes
steps.body: Recheck pressure after each small model-approved adjustment and under flow.

safeChecks: Use a known working pressure gauge.
Record which fixtures are open during the flowing test.
Return the locknut or cap exactly as the model requires.
stopConditions: The valve serves a complex commercial system
notThisDevice: Adjustment does not fix an undersized service line.
Pressure rise from a closed-system water heater may involve thermal expansion.
A backflow test gauge procedure is different.
evidenceNote: The interactive reading is a screening result. Follow the exact manufacturer instruction and applicable local code.
